entries.appliesTo: any person who intentionally discloses or threatens to disclose a private intimate image without consent

sources.prohibition: § 15-75-320(A) — 'a depicted individual who is identifiable and who suffers harm from a person's intentional disclosure or threatened disclosure of an intimate image that was private without the depicted individual's consent has a cause of action against the person'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 15-75-320(A) — 'a depicted individual who is identifiable and who suffers harm' (no age limitation; § 15-75-360(C) tolls the limitations period for 'a depicted individual who was a child')
sources.penaltyMax: § 15-75-350(A)(1)(b) — 'statutory damages not to exceed ten thousand dollars against each defendant found liable under this article for all disclosure and threatened disclosures by the defendant'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 15-75-350(A)(1)(b) — 'against each defendant found liable under this article'
sources.enforcer: § 15-75-320(A) — 'has a cause of action against the person'

flags: civil-remedies act, not a criminal prohibition — no criminal penalties anywhere in the text; category 'criminal' used because the act binds persons with a conduct prohibition and creates no ongoing company compliance duty, and rule 10 routes NCII conduct prohibitions to ai-crimes

intimate-image definition reaches AI deepfakes: § 15-75-310(9)(a) covers images 'generated or substantially modified using machine learning techniques or any other computer-generated or machine-generated means to falsely depict an individual's appearance or conduct' alongside authentic photographs/film/video

platform safe harbor, not a duty: § 15-75-330(E) — 'A covered platform that is in compliance with the Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act of 2025, P.L. No. 119-12, is not liable under this article'

remedies beyond statutory damages: greater of actual damages or the $10,000 statutory cap, plus disgorgement (§ 15-75-350(A)(2) 'an amount equal to any monetary gain made by the defendant'), punitive damages (§ 15-75-350(A)(3)), attorney's fees and injunctive relief (§ 15-75-350(B))
limitations: 3 years from discovery for disclosure, 4 years for a threat to disclose (§ 15-75-360(A)); tolled until age eighteen for child plaintiffs (§ 15-75-360(C))
construction clauses: consistent with 47 U.S.C. § 230 and no alteration of sovereign immunity (§ 15-75-370)
